s: in front of, ahead of (relative location in space)
before, prior to, ahead of (relative location in time)
ago (location in the past relative to the present)
from, against (a threat or negative outcome)
Er konnte vor dem Tsunami nicht mehr fliehen.
Du hast mich vorm Ertrinken gerettet.
vor.et: From Middle High German vore, vor, from Old High German fora. Cognate with Dutch voor. Compare English fore.

s: pre- (denotes primarily that something is before or in front of another thing or higher in a hierarchy)
Separable verbal prefix indicating a presentation or performance
vor- + singen (“to sing”) → vorsingen (“to audition (by singing)”)
vor- + sprechen (“to speak”) → vorsprechen (“to audition (by reciting)”)
vor-.et: From Middle High German vor-, vore-, from Old High German fora-, furi-, from Proto-West Germanic *forē-. Cognate with English fore-.
